reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Probability.Predictable
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: a predictable process (Z in H^2_W "predictable"; "Z, U already predictable"; the
predictable version Theta^- with left limits): a map (time) x Omega -> (a measurable space,
R^{m x d} etc.) measurable with respect to the predictable sigma-field P of the setting's
filtration (and the Borel sigma-algebra of the target). Faithful Lean: Predictable F X :=
Measurable[predictableSigma F] (uncurried X). The same caveats about the time-0 generators as for
predictableSigma. Every left-continuous adapted process (in particular X_{t-}) must be
Predictable under the definition.

comparison.text:
Lean: Predictable F H := StronglyMeasurable[predictableSigma F] (fun p : R x Omega => H p.2 p.1),
for H : Omega -> R -> F with F a topological space with zero.
Comparison with the locked reading: measurability with respect to the predictable sigma-field
of the setting's filtration, of the uncurried process; for the paper's targets (R^{m x d},
Euclidean spaces, separable metrizable) strong measurability is equivalent to Borel
measurability; for a general target it is the right notion (limits of simple functions). The
time-0 slice is standard (initial cell (-inf,0] x A, A in F 0), so a process with an
F_0-measurable random time-0 value is predictable; left-continuous adapted processes are
predictable (the generators are the standard ones). Predictable implies ProgressivelyMeasurable
(Predictable.progressivelyMeasurable, under the convention F constant on (-inf,0]).
Representation choices: time axis R; curried order Omega -> R -> F. Harmless.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: (1) strong measurability for predictableSigma (equivalent to Borel
measurability for the paper's finite-dimensional targets); (2) time axis R and the conventions of
predictableSigma (standard on [0,T], time-0 slice F_0-measurable); (3) curried order
Omega -> R -> F.
